To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we identified a combination of three genes that is most suitable to be used as reference for qRT- PCR analysis in NFPA tissue, and (2) we found that the frequently used ACTB is not the most stable gene and that its use should be avoided.
We evaluated the expression stability of 10 candidate reference genes in 30 NFPA samples and found that YWHAZ, TUBA 1B and SDHA are most stable in NFPA samples.

the following ten candidate reference genes were evaluated for their expression stability in human NFPs: ACTB, GAPDH, B2M and RPLP0 were found to be unstable, while the remaining six genes, namely, HPRT1 and UBC were found to be stable and YWHAZ, HMBS and TUBA1 were found to be the most stable reference genes in this particular tissue type.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the validation of candidate reference genes for use in qPCR studies in NFPA.
the validation of candidate reference genes for expression analysis in NFPA tissue.
evaluating the most suitable reference genes for qPCR analysis in NFPAs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, in human NFPA samples: 1) RPLP0 and YWHAZ are the most stable reference genes, 2) SDHA and TUBA1A are the least stable reference genes, and 3) the most stable combination of reference genes is RPLP0/YWHAZ/ACTB/B2M/UBC.
the most stable reference genes for expression analysis in NFPA are B2M and UBC.
the best combination for normalizing gene expression levels in human NFPA tissue is a combination of the three most stable genes, namely, ACTB, HPRT1 and RPLP0.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
RefFinder ranked B2M as the most stably expressed gene in NFPA samples followed by ACTB.
the most stable gene in human NFPA was ACTB, followed by GAPDH, HPRT1 and RPLP0.
the most stable gene for qPCR normalization is UBC and the second most stable gene is GAPDH.
The main takeaway from our work is that
no one reference gene is the most stable for all samples.
no single gene can be recommended as the best candidate reference gene for NFPA.
there is no one single reference gene that can be considered as a universal reference for all NFPA patients.
